# Overall Project Weekly Summary (Apr 12 - 18, 2026)

This week, Optimism focused on hardening the core infrastructure that powers the Superchain, specifically by streamlining how the network handles upgrades and improving the reliability of its node software. By consolidating technical tasks and modernizing build processes, the team has cleared significant technical debt, paving the way for safer and more efficient protocol evolutions.

## Executive Summary
The primary achievement this week was the completion of the "Network Upgrade Transaction" (NUT) bundle system, which simplifies how the network executes protocol changes. Alongside this, a major architectural cleanup of the Docker build pipeline and the Proxyd service has significantly improved the stability and maintainability of the entire OP Stack.

### Key Strategic Initiatives & Outcomes

**Simplifying Protocol Upgrades**
*Goal: To make it easier and safer to deploy network-wide updates without manual intervention.*
*   Completed the "NUT" bundle work for `op-node`, allowing the system to read and execute upgrade instructions directly from standardized JSON files ([ethereum-optimism/ecosystem](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/ecosystem)).
*   Consolidated multiple development tracks for `kona-node` into a single roadmap, ensuring a more unified approach to managing Layer 2 chain upgrades ([ethereum-optimism/superchain-ops](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/superchain-ops)).

**Strengthening Infrastructure Reliability**
*Goal: To ensure the network remains online and performant even during high traffic or regional outages.*
*   Overhauled the consensus architecture for **Proxyd**, improving how the system communicates with Ethereum to ensure data remains accurate and consistent ([ethereum-optimism/infra](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/infra)).
*   Engaged in a strategic architectural debate regarding "Sequencer Redundancy." The team is prioritizing the use of industry-standard tools (like Nginx or HAProxy) to handle failovers, ensuring the core code remains lean and maintainable ([ethereum-optimism/op-geth](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/op-geth)).

**Preparing for Future Network Hardforks**
*Goal: To integrate the latest Ethereum improvements and Optimism-specific features into the protocol.*
*   Added foundational support for the upcoming **Osaka and Jovian** upgrades, including new technical "opcodes" and gas limit protections that keep the network secure ([ethereum-optimism/optimism](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism)).
*   Refined the "EL-Sync" process to fix long-standing user experience issues where nodes would occasionally struggle to find their place during initial synchronization ([ethereum-optimism/optimism](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism)).

### Cross-Repository Coordination
*   **Unified Build System**: A coordinated effort across nearly all repositories (Ecosystem, Infra, Superchain-ops, and Geth) migrated Docker build configurations to a centralized `images.json` system. This ensures that every piece of the Optimism stack is built using the same high standards and security checks.
*   **L2 Chain Management (L2CM)**: Development of the L2CM system required synchronized updates between the `optimism` core repository and the `superchain-ops` repository to ensure that new "Fault Proof" tests and upgrade mechanisms work seamlessly together.

## Repository Spotlights

### ethereum-optimism/optimism
*   Implemented support for several new Ethereum Improvement Proposals (EIPs) for the Osaka/Jovian hardforks ([#20071](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/20071), [#20073](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/20073)).
*   Improved node synchronization by allowing `op-node` to better handle "safe" and "finalized" states during initial setup ([#19972](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/19972)).
*   Migrated critical Interop Fault Proof tests to a more robust testing suite to ensure cross-chain security ([#20047](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/20047)).

### ethereum-optimism/infra
*   Launched a new consensus architecture for Proxyd to enhance backend reliability ([#597](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/infra/pull/597)).
*   Centralized the Docker build matrix into a single configuration file to reduce technical debt and speed up development ([#603](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/infra/pull/603)).

### ethereum-optimism/superchain-ops
*   Successfully performed scheduled security maintenance by rotating authorized signers for the network ([#1394](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/superchain-ops/pull/1394)).
*   Finalized the integration of NUT transactions for `op-node`, a key milestone for automated protocol upgrades ([#18835](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/superchain-ops/issues/18835)).

### ethereum-optimism/ethereum-optimism.github.io
*   Expanded the Base ecosystem by adding metadata for new tokens including FYRE and AFUK ([#1302](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/ethereum-optimism.github.io/pull/1302), [#1301](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/ethereum-optimism.github.io/pull/1301)).
*   Updated the project's publishing security by adopting a "trusted publisher" model for software releases ([#1304](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/ethereum-optimism.github.io/pull/1304)).
